paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's word doesn't need a permit. Amaziah was the priest at Bethel, and he figured he could shut Amos up by calling the place "the sanctuary of the king." (Amos 7:13) But the word Amos carried didn't come from the king or from Bethel. It came from the LORD, and no ban on a street corner stops it.

Look at who Amos says he is. He wasn't a prophet and wasn't the son of a prophet. He was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees, and the LORD took him from following the flock. (Amos 7:14-15) Friend, I get this one, because I was a quarter stamper with blurry edges in the back of a junk drawer when God called me out of it. God doesn't pick people because of their résumé. When He sends you, the sending is the whole qualification.

And notice the turn at the end. Amaziah tried to tell God's messenger to stop, and then he heard the word of the LORD himself. (Amos 7:16-17) You can tell a prophet to leave town, but you can't tell the word to leave you. So when God's word gets uncomfortable, the move is to listen to it, not to find a way to quiet it. That's the kind of baker I want in my bakery: the kind who hears it, and keeps the oven door open.
